title: Maximum Subarray
corePattern: Kadane's Algorithm - Dynamic Programming with Running Best and Reset on Negative Prefix
interviewTips: Ask if subarray must be non-empty: for all-negative input like [-1,-2] answer is -1, not 0.
Trade-off to discuss: Brute Force O(n^2) vs Divide and Conquer O(n log n) vs Kadane O(n) O(1) - why Kadane dominates for this problem.
Edge-case tip: initialize answer to nums[0] not 0, and test single element, all negative, and large mixed array.

approaches.name: Approach 1: Brute Force Enumeration
approaches.intuition: Try every possible subarray defined by start i and end j, compute its sum and keep the maximum seen.
approaches.theory: Any subarray is determined by its left and right indices. Fix left i, expand right j incrementally maintaining running sum cur = sum(nums[i..j]). Compare cur to global best. This enumerates all n*(n+1)/2 subarrays, so the maximum must be found.

timeComplexity.explanation: n starts, up to n ends per start, each extension O(1) with running sum, total O(n^2).

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only two integer variables cur and best besides input.

steps: i=0: cur sequence -2, -1, -4 -> best stays -1 after j=1
i=3: cur sequence 4, 3, 5, 6, 1, 5 -> best updates to 6
i=4 onward: no larger sum found

edgeCases: All negative [-2,-1] returns -1, requires init to nums[0]
Large n=1e5 will TLE, motivates optimal solution

approaches.name: Approach 2: Divide and Conquer
approaches.intuition: Split array in half. Best subarray is either entirely left, entirely right, or crossing the middle. Solve left and right recursively and compute crossing best by expanding from middle.
approaches.theory: Let mid divide [l,r]. Recursively get leftBest and rightBest. For crossing case, max suffix ending at mid plus max prefix starting at mid+1 gives max crossing sum, found by linear scans outward from mid. Answer is max of the three. Recurrence T(n)=2T(n/2)+O(n) gives O(n log n).

timeComplexity.explanation: Two recursive halves plus O(n) linear scan for crossing sum at each level, depth log n.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Recursion stack depth log n for balanced splits, no extra arrays.

steps: left recursion returns 9, right recursion returns 15
cross: best suffix left = 8 (5+4-1), best prefix right = 15 (7+8), cross=23

edgeCases: Single element base case returns nums[l]
All negative: crossing sum correctly picks least negative suffix plus prefix
Recursion depth ~17 for n=1e5, safe in all languages

approaches.name: Approach 3: Kadane's Algorithm (Optimal)
approaches.intuition: Scan once keeping best subarray ending at current position. Either extend previous subarray or start fresh at current element if previous sum is negative.
approaches.theory: Define dp[i] = max subarray sum ending at i. Then dp[i] = max(nums[i], dp[i-1]+nums[i]) because any subarray ending at i is either just nums[i] or previous best ending at i-1 extended. Global answer = max dp[i]. Only previous dp needed, so O(1) space. This is greedy reset: discard negative prefix.

timeComplexity.explanation: Single left-to-right pass, O(1) work per element.

spaceComplexity.explanation: Only cur for ending-here best and best for global answer.

edgeCases: All negative [-3,-2,-1]: cur resets each time, best stays -1
